board.name: South Carolina Board of Medical Examiners (LLR), advised by the Physician Assistant Committee

licence.title: Physician Assistant (PA)
licence.renewalDeadline: December 31 of odd-numbered years (current licence period ends December 31, 2027); late renewal allowed for one year after expiry, then reactivation

ce.hoursNote: South Carolina sets no state CME hour total for PAs. The renewal requirement is an active NCCPA certification (NCCPA's own rules then govern CME and PANRE). The only state hour mandate is 4 hours of controlled substance CE every two years for PAs with controlled substance prescriptive authority.
ce.categoryRules: None set by the state; follows NCCPA

topicMandates.topic: Approved procedures of prescribing and monitoring Schedule II, III and IV controlled substances
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs with controlled substance prescriptive authority

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 4 hours every two years on prescribing and monitoring Schedules II to IV (S.C. Code 40-47-965(B)(2)); plus federal DEA one-time 8 hour SUD training (MATE)

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written scope of practice guidelines signed by all supervising physicians and the PA, on file at all practice sites, submitted to the board (PA may start 10 business days after submission while the board decides). Changes to supervising physicians or added acts are submitted to the board through the PA Scope of Practice Guidelines Portal. Guidelines record dates reviewed and amended; no fixed review interval is stated in the statute.
practice.notes: A PA with under two years continuous practice, or changing specialty, needs 60 days on site with the supervising physician before practising off site (waivable in writing). Bills to replace supervision (S.44, H.3579, S.669) were introduced in 2025 and did not advance past committee.

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: Prescribing is authorized through the scope of practice guidelines. Controlled substance prescriptive authority requires board approval with pharmacotherapeutics education, a South Carolina controlled substance registration (DPH, formerly DHEC) and a DEA registration. Schedule II narcotic: initial prescription limited to a five day supply. The SC controlled substance registration renews annually, due April 1 for PA-C registrants.
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 4 hours every two years on prescribing and monitoring Schedules II to IV

board.name: South Carolina State Board of Nursing (LLR)

rn.renewalDeadline: All nursing licences expire April 30 of every even-numbered year (next April 30, 2028)
rn.ceNote: 30 contact hours is one of FOUR alternatives, not a fixed requirement: 30 contact hours from a board recognized provider; OR maintained national certification; OR an academic nursing program; OR employer verification of competency. An NP who keeps national certification meets RN and APRN competency without the 30 hours. Records kept 4 years; produce within 5 business days of an audit request.

aprn.title: APRN (NP, CNM, CNS, CRNA); nurse practitioner licensed as APRN-NP
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: Separate South Carolina APRN licence on top of the RN licence; a multistate RN privilege qualifies but an SC APRN licence is still required. Prescriptive authority is a separate board authorization with its own identification number.
aprn.ceNote: Same continued competency alternatives as RN (national certification counts, and is required anyway for APRNs). NPs with prescriptive authority add 20 pharmacotherapeutics contact hours every two years (2 on controlled substances if they hold CS authority).

topicMandates.topic: Prescribing controlled substances (within the 20 pharmacotherapeutics hours)
topicMandates.appliesTo: NPs with controlled substance prescriptive authority

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: Yes. Prescriptive authority is a separate board application (initially 45 contact hours of pharmacotherapeutics within two years, 15 of them on controlled substances if prescribing Schedules II to V); valid two years, expiring with the APRN licence. Controlled substances also need the SC DPH controlled substance registration (annual, due April 1 for APRNs) and DEA.
prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: 20 contact hours of pharmacotherapeutics every two years
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 of the 20 pharmacotherapeutics hours on prescribing controlled substances, every two years; plus federal DEA one-time 8 hour SUD training (MATE)

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written practice agreement with a physician who is readily available for consultation. Reviewed, dated and signed at least annually; produced to the board within 72 hours of request; random board audit at least biennially. Notify the board within 15 business days of a change of practice setting or physician. The NP must also spend a portion of practice time in an underserved or rural area or serving an underserved population (40-33-34(C)).

unverified: S.C. Code Regs. ch. 91 (Board of Nursing) not loaded; APRN renewal rules come from the statute and the board's APRN page.
Whether the APRN renewal form itself asks for proof of national certification was not confirmed from the form; the statute requires certification to be maintained.
'Restricted' practice authority is our classification of the statute (physician practice agreement required for medical acts); the statute does not use that word.
No SC rule found that accepts NCCPA CME in place of the 4 controlled substance hours; treat the 4 hours as separate.
verificationCorrections: PA 4 hour controlled substance CE: confirmed at 40-47-965(B)(2); noted the board CE PDF mis-cites it as (B)[3]; added renewal form attestation fact.
SC controlled substance registration: resolved the researcher's unverified item; it renews annually, due April 1 for APRN and PA-C, no grace period (Reg 60-4; DPH Drug Control Renewals page).

RN/APRN 30 contact hours: clarified that 30 hours is one of four alternatives (national certification, academic program, employer verification); added ceAlternatives so the app does not show 30 hours as mandatory for certified NPs.
NP practice: added the statutory requirement to spend a portion of time in an underserved or rural area or population (40-33-34(C)).
NP prescribing: added Schedule II non-narcotic 30 day supply limit (40-33-34(F)(1)(d)).
Added PA late renewal window (through December 31, 2026, then reactivation) and the 2026 nursing renewal window; confirmed 40-33-34 current through 2024 Act 120.
Pending bills H.3579, H.3580, S.44, S.45, S.669 re-checked: still only referred to committee.
